,FIFTH AVENUE, NEW YORK, CELEBRATES IT'S CENTERNIAL
AMIVERSARY,--SECEPERS NORN BY A DARE.

#371709-10- One of the Many interesting Anniversary Exhibits in Store Windows on fifth Avenue, was the one of Old and New Shoes and Slippers in the store of J. & J. Slater. Photo shows the tiny slippers worn by a dwarf servant of the Fred Bishop of Prague, Bosnia during the yrs of 1815-20. Thus the tiny silpper is over a century old.

LOS ANGELES DANCER CHOSEN TO DEAR
PEACCOCK BATHING SUIT.

Fay Parrish, the beautiful Los Angeles dancer from the Roscoff School was chosen to wear the exquisite Peacock model bathing suit which created a stir at the Revue Des Modes recently. This model designed by Mrs. Harold Ryerson was made of white silk jersey embroidered by hand in colored yarns and beads and edged with silver fringe.

RUSSIAN BOOTS' ALL THE VOGUE.

It is perfectly proper to be Russian-booted. In fact if you are not, you are not in the swim, as far as style is concerned. All the fair damsels, who know what's what, are wearing them, and that seems to be all necessary to make it popular. The boot has a unique design, and fits loosely about the foot.

THEY BLOCKED ALL TRAFFIC in King and Elizabeth Streets Sydney, when the popular young Australian actress, Gladys Moncrieff, married Mr Thomas Moore at It James Church, King Street on May 20. The crowd separated bride and groom as they left the church, and the police had to bring them together again. Mr & Mrs Moore leave for England shortly. Photo shows the bride and widowroom.

WINNERS IN BEAUTY SHOW FASHION REVUE--AND MOB SCENE
----AT CONEY ISLAND EASTER SUNDAY.

S378,623 Otho Cushing presents the prizes to the four girls who survived Coney Island's record mob scene on the Broadwalk Easter Sunday with -out a single black eye. Fifty cops and 50 xBoy Stout tried to escort 50 beauties in fifty beautiful costumes down the Boardwalk. The crowd present not only smashed all records but also smashed the rope held by the Scots, smashed hats,parasols,slippers, and parcels(hip) and caused a lot of folks to smash the Command against profane swearing. So the Fair Fifty were taken, somewhat ruffled but still game, to the roof of the Child's Building and there, 75 feet above the Four Million (or more), these four were picked as the prize winners and awarded(left to right)--Hope Thompson, pearl necklace as most beautiful; Dora Ampey, silver cup as most fashionable; Peggy-Shannon, a parasol; and Laurette Rehm, a silk bathing suit
